claude.sample_unit: GPT-5 responses (10 base prompt topics x 4 conditions)

links.outcome: Interrater reliability of rater-coded perceived factuality, stance, and safety notices
links.effect: Perceived factuality ICC(2,k)=-0.16; stance orientation Fleiss κ=0.17; safety notice κ=-0.02; ratings not verified against a gold standard. Citation presence κ=0.84.
links.quote: Ratings were not verified against a gold-standard reference.

links.outcome: Citation presence when peer-reviewed citations requested; citation validity not verified
links.effect: Citations present in 19/20 (95%) evidence-required vs 5/20 (25%) no-evidence responses; authenticity of references not verified, so hallucinated citations could not be excluded.
links.quote: Nineteen out of 20 (95%) evidence-required responses contained citations, compared with 5 out of 20 (25%) no-evidence responses.

unlisted_practices: Prompt framing (patient-centered vs skill-centered) to steer stance of LLM educational responses
Prompting the LLM to cite peer-reviewed research to increase citation inclusion
Teaching students and faculty to verify AI-generated citations (PMID/DOI) as part of AI literacy

links.effect: Safety notice κ=−0.02; perceived factuality ICC (2,k)=−0.16.
links.quote: Safety notice flags showed no meaningful agreement (κ=−0.02), as did perceived factuality ratings [ICC (2,k)=−0.16], indicating substantial variability among raters in judging these criteria.

links.effect: Citations appeared in 19/20 (95%) evidence-required responses versus 5/20 (25%) no-evidence responses.
links.quote: Evidence-required prompts produced citations in 19 out of 20 (95%) responses, whereas no-evidence prompts produced citations in 5 out of 20 (25%) responses.

unlisted_practices: Prompt instruction to cite peer-reviewed dental research
Patient-centered versus skill-centered instructional framing for dental education prompts
Instructional framing in prompt design (patient-centered vs skill-centered framing)
Explicit evidence requirement instructions in prompts (instructing generative models to cite peer-reviewed research)
